Address the code scanning alerts raised on the promotion

## Problem and related issue / 问题与关联 Issue

CodeQL raised four alerts on the promotion PR #61, in code from #43, #45 and #52.

## Resulting behavior / 改动后的行为

- `internal/browser/steps.go` (potentially unsafe quoting): a select step's value was spliced into the JavaScript run in the page. JSON is a valid expression and Go escapes U+2028/U+2029, so it could not break out, but the value now travels as a `Runtime.callFunctionOn` argument and never touches the source.
- `internal/app/avatar_uploads.go` (path from user input): the existence check joined a reference's file name into a path and relied on its callers having validated it (they do: a 64-hex sha256 `.png`). It now checks the name itself and joins only its base name.
- `internal/provider/discover.go`, `probe.go` (request to a user-provided URL): requesting the gateway address the user typed is the feature, so any host stays allowed; the address must now be an `http` or `https` URL with a host (no `file:`, no bare path).

- Also: the approval-cards E2E spec (`m5-acceptance`) timed out twice on CI after #53 landed. Resolving a ChatGPT-account member's model asked the profile's control engine for its default model, under a lock, on every turn; where that engine had to start first, several members' turns queued behind it. The lookup was redundant (`turnModel` already names the default from the team's own engine right before the turn), so `MemberModel` no longer touches an engine.

## Validation / 验证

- `scripts/check.sh` passes. The real-browser test (`TestRealBrowserDrivesAPage`, which includes a select step) passes on Edge. New `TestOnlyWebAddressesAreRequested` for the address check.
- The request-forgery alerts are expected to remain: the endpoint is the user's own configuration on a loopback-only local app, and no allow-list can name a gateway in advance.

## Compatibility and data impact / 兼容性与数据影响

A provider address without `http://` or `https://` is now refused when fetching or checking models. No migration.

## Review checklist / 检查

- [x] The change is focused and relevant checks passed, or failures are explained. / 改动聚焦，相关检查通过或已说明失败。
- [x] Compatibility, user data, upgrade and rollback effects are assessed above. / 已说明兼容性、用户数据、升级与回滚影响。
- [x] Relevant UI text is available in English and Chinese. / 涉及的界面文案已覆盖中英文。
- [x] No credentials, private AI instructions, runtime data or raw traces are included. / 未包含凭据、私人 AI 指令、运行数据或原始 trace。
- [x] I have the right to submit this material under Apache-2.0 and preserved third-party attribution. / 有权按 Apache-2.0 提交并保留第三方声明。

fix: restore checksum updates in autofix and fix aqua upa for v2.65.0 or later

This pull request fixes two issues.

## 1. Checksums are no longer updated by autofix

Since #5431, the autofix workflow no longer updated checksum files (`aqua-checksums.json`), because that pull request replaced the workflow steps with go-autofix-action's reusable workflow and dropped the steps running `aqua upc -prune` and `pinact run -u`.

This pull request adds a reusable workflow `.github/workflows/wc_autofix.yaml` and calls it from `autofix.yaml`. It runs the Go autofix workflow (`suzuki-shunsuke/go-autofix-action`) and a job that:

- Runs `aqua upc -prune` in `pkg/cosign`, `pkg/slsa`, `pkg/minisign`, `pkg/ghattestation`, `pkg/packslip`, and `tests/pnpm`
- Runs `pinact run -u` for the documents in `website/docs`
- Commits the changes with `autofix-ci/action`

Outdated checksums in `pkg/packslip/aqua-checksums.json` and an outdated action version in `website/docs/guides/checksum.md` are also updated.

## 2. `aqua upa` fails to update aqua to v2.65.0 or later

This is a bug in v2.65.0. aqua no longer releases SLSA Provenance since v2.65.0, but `aqua upa` still tried to verify it, so updating aqua to v2.65.0 or later failed.

`InstallAqua` in `pkg/installpackage/aqua.go` no longer verifies SLSA Provenance for v2.65.0 or later. SLSA Provenance is still verified for versions from v2.17.0 to v2.64.x via a new version override.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

benchmarks.task_description:
A deleted cluster gives back the global backup slots its backups hold (#2135)

Fixes #2135

## Problem

A cluster deleted while one of its backups runs kept its global backup slot until replication-manager restarted: the slot is given back when the cluster's own monitor loop sees WARN0175 / WARN0073 resolve, and `DeleteCluster` stops that loop. With every slot taken this way, every backup of every cluster waits in WARN0174 with no timeout (default `backup-concurrent-slots` = 1). A child or staging cluster starts a logical backup right after its seed, so a child deleted shortly after its creation hits it.

## Change

Each cluster counts the global slots its backups hold (`backupSlotsHeld`):

- `waitForBackupSlot` counts the slot it takes; a cluster that is stopping gives back a slot that frees instead of keeping it.
- `releaseBackupSlot` gives a slot back only when the cluster holds one. The four release points use it: WARN0073 / WARN0175 resolution, the two early exits of the physical backup, the backup verification. A state that resolves on a cluster holding no slot no longer frees another cluster's.
- `Cluster.Stop` gives back every slot the cluster still holds.

A deleted cluster's backup can run a few seconds after its slot is given back, until its servers are gone.

## Tests

- Unit (`cluster/server_globals_test.go`): `Stop` gives back the cluster's slots and keeps another cluster's; a release with no slot held frees none; a stopping cluster keeps no slot. Each fails without its part of the change. `go test ./cluster/` passes.
- Lab, MariaDB 10.11, 2 slots, no restart between steps, through the API (create-child, delete as soon as the child's post-seed backup starts):
  - develop without the change: 1/2 after the first delete, 2/2 after the second, then the parent's backup waits in WARN0174;
  - develop with the change: 0/2 after each of two deletes; a logical and a physical backup of the parent take a slot and give it back;
  - fix/splitdump-child-seed-gtid-2124 with the same change applied locally: the same results, and `testCreateChildSplitdump` and `testCreateStagingSplitdump` pass with 0/2 after.

## What
Restores the README key-table row `| \`j\` \`down\` | focus the next pane |`.

## Why
#422 reworded that row to mention the footer skip, but `TestKeyTablesAgree` (`sdk/mono/cmd`) requires each README key row to match `app.Keys`' help text verbatim. `Run Unit Tests` failed on #422's run and is now red on `main` (`4427e2f`).

## Impact
Docs only. The fixed-pane skip stays documented in the `panes[].zoomable` row of the config table.

## Testing
`go vet ./... && go test -race -count=1 ./...` in `sdk/mono`: all 10 packages ok (reproduced the failure on `main` first).
